title: Jeremiah Smith trolled Texas with 'Horns Down' after huge Ohio State TD
description: Well, it was inevitable.
fullText:
Ohio State superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith knew exactly how to troll Texas after scoring a touchdown right before halftime in Austin on Saturday night.

At the tail end of a brutal half for the Longhorns, the Buckeyes got a last-minute touchdown on a beautiful catch from Smith.

TEXAS: Arch Manning's perplexed reaction to this improbable INT was priceless

After he got Ohio State that key touchdown, he broke out the infamous "Horns Down" hand motion to mock the Texas fans in the stands.

Of course, there's no better way to poke fun at Texas than with the "Horns Down," which isn't penalized in the SEC. Opponents have free reign over the hand signal, and they take advantage of it.

title: Oklahoma Ball Boy Goes Viral After Chasing Michigan Defender
description: Oklahoma's ball boy became an unexpected viral star during Michigan's 17-10 win. His determined attempt to retrieve the football from Troy Bowles quickly drew attention online.
fullText:
Michigan and Oklahoma produced plenty of serious football Saturday afternoon. Somehow, one of the most memorable sequences involved a guy who never played a snap.

During Michigan's 17-10 victory over No. 11 Oklahoma, Wolverines linebacker Troy Bowles recovered a second-quarter fumble and headed toward the Michigan sideline with the football. An Oklahoma ball boy apparently had one objective: get that ball back.

The resulting pursuit quickly became one of the game's viral moments.

The video below shows the Oklahoma ball boy following Bowles down the Michigan sideline, repeatedly attempting to reclaim the Sooners' football while Bowles kept moving. The effort level was unquestionable. The leverage situation was considerably less favorable.

The scene followed one of Michigan's biggest defensive plays of the first half.

Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer connected with Parker Livingstone before Chris Bracy knocked the football loose. Bowles recovered it, giving Michigan the game's first takeaway. A detailed account of the play credited Bracy with forcing the fumble and Bowles with recovering it.

Bowles had already emerged as an important piece of Michigan's defense after recording 12 tackles against Western Michigan. The matchup with Oklahoma also came after defensive end Dom Nichols delivered a pointed message about containing Mateer entering the game.

Michigan's defense backed up much of that confidence. The Wolverines held Oklahoma to 289 total yards and forced two turnovers in the victory, including Jyaire Hill's fourth-quarter interception that helped set up Jordan Marshall's go-ahead touchdown.

Much of the attention entering Saturday had been on Bryce Underwood, whose development became a major topic after the Western Michigan opener. Urban Meyer had specifically pointed to Underwood's processing and progression work before the Oklahoma game.

Underwood answered some of those questions. Michigan's defense answered plenty more.

And somewhere in the middle of it, Oklahoma's ball boy provided a reminder that every member of the traveling party apparently has an assignment.

Even when the assignment turns into chasing a 224-pound Big Ten linebacker down the opposing sideline.

title: Iowa basketball hosting Cayden Daughtry, Cole Kelly on key visits
description: It's a huge recruiting weekend for Ben McCollum and the Iowa basketball program.
fullText:
The Cy-Hawk football game is always a big recruiting weekend for Kirk Ferentz's program. This year, it isn't just the football program that's welcoming some big-name recruits to Iowa City for the game. Ben McCollum and the men's basketball program will be doing the same.

Since McCollum took the head coaching job at Iowa 18 months ago, he's done a fantastic job recruiting. Whether it's the high school level or the transfer portal, the Hawkeyes have seen a massive influx of talent in the last year-plus.

McCollum and the Hawkeyes are hosting a pair of elite, program-changing prospects this weekend. Five-star point guard Cayden Daughtry and four-star small forward Cole Kelly will be at Kinnick Stadium on Saturday night on visits.

5⭐️ Cayden Daughtry is currently on his official visit to Iowa, source told @Rivals. 

The 6-foot point guard is the No. 6 overall recruit in the 2027 class, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings. https://t.co/a9TcFI3ojg https://t.co/Qa3hh50Kpv pic.twitter.com/Wnsw82cZhe

Daughtry is the big fish that every blue-blood program is chasing right now. He's the third-best prospect in the entire 2027 recruiting class, according to 247Sports. The 6-foot guard from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, lit up Nike's Peach Jam this summer and would be a massive get for McCollum.

Daughtry visited Florida State two weeks ago and Tennessee last Saturday. He's set to visit Florida, Miami, and Arkansas over the next few months. Daughtry trimmed his list of schools to 14 on Aug. 26, but it seems like UConn has been removed from that list. On3's Joe Tipton reported that Daughtry will no longer visit UConn after the Huskies added the commitment from NaVorro Bowman Jr.

Kelly is a fast-riser in the 2028 recruiting class. The 6-foot-6 wing is listed as the 34th-best prospect in the 2028 class, according to 247Sports. A native of Naperville, Ill., Kelly visited Purdue over the summer. Other Big Ten schools such as Illinois, Indiana, Nebraska, and Ohio State have made offers. This is a big opportunity for McCollum to make his pitch.

Joining those two in attendance will be Keller Daugherty. The four-star 2027 forward committed to Iowa back in June and will help McCollum try to land Daughtry and Kelly.

McCollum has racked up a lot of victories on and off the court in his short tenure in Iowa City so far. He'll look to win a few more battles this weekend.

title: Tyrese Haliburton Trolls Alleged 49ers Impostor With Custom Jersey
description: Tyrese Haliburton joined in on the Daejon Love story by holding up a 49ers jersey with Love's name across the back during his stream.
fullText:
Tyrese Haliburton held up a San Francisco 49ers jersey with Love's name across the back on his stream, a night after the 49ers opened the season with a 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams at Melbourne Cricket Ground.

"He didn't play last night, he on IR," Haliburton said.

No NFL team has ever employed Daejon Labrayae Love. Federal agents arrested him Aug. 24 in Boise, Idaho, along with 18-year-old Taylor Jamie Chan. Both are charged in Portland, Oregon, with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud.

Since February 2022, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Oregon, the two took about $1.3 million from more than two dozen women in Oregon, Washington, Idaho, and California. Love, 35, met most of them on dating apps. He told them he played wide receiver for the 49ers. Other times he was a wealthy real estate investor. Chan played the financial adviser. The charges are accusations, and neither man has been convicted.

The Indiana Pacers guard has been on the story for close to two weeks. He posted about Love's videos on X on Sept. 1.

"Daejon Love's digital footprint insane, I ain't seen the same video twice," Haliburton explained.

Haliburton has not played a game in 14 months. He tore his right Achilles tendon on a non-contact drive in the first quarter of Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals on June 22, 2025, with Indiana and Oklahoma City tied 16-16, and had surgery the next day. Pacers president Kevin Pritchard ruled him out for the season on July 7, 2025. Indiana finished 19-63.

Rehabilitation ran into a second problem in the winter, when Haliburton was diagnosed with facial shingles on Feb. 22. He was doing full-court 4-on-4 against team interns and reserves by late January. Chris Haynes reported in July that Indiana expected to have him for Day 1. Haliburton said Aug. 12 that his rehabilitation was finished and that he needed no more time.

"If the season was today, I'd be ready," Haliburton said.

Pacers coach Rick Carlisle has had him in five-on-five work for months.

"It's going to be a bit of a journey for him," Carlisle said after Indiana's Summer League win over Cleveland.

ESPN's Jamal Collier wrote that Indiana may take it slow with Haliburton at the start of the season. NBA 2K27 rates him a 90 overall, down from the 93 he carried in NBA 2K26.

Haliburton and Brock Purdy were at Iowa State at the same time, Haliburton running the basketball program and Purdy the football program. Before Super Bowl LVIII, Haliburton said he was pulling for Purdy and San Francisco.

Purdy threw three touchdown passes in Melbourne and was not sacked on 34 attempts. Mike Evans caught a two-yard touchdown on the opening drive of the third quarter, his first with San Francisco. Renardo Green intercepted Matthew Stafford in the second quarter at the San Francisco 14-yard line. It was the first regular-season NFL game played in Australia and the fourth season opener between the two teams.

Haliburton is not the only one working the Love material. Rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling switched his number from 15 to 7, the number Love wore in his workout videos. San Francisco wide receivers coach Leonard Hankerson posted an AI-generated photo of himself coaching Love at a 49ers practice. The Cleveland Guardians put Love in a lineup graphic on X on Aug. 29.

Indiana's roster looks different from the one Haliburton left. Myles Turner signed with Milwaukee and Bennedict Mathurin left for New Orleans. Ivica Zubac is at center now, and Kelly Oubre Jr. was added on the wing.

Haliburton averaged 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 9.2 assists in 73 games in 2024-25, his last full season. He added 1.4 steals a game, shot 47.3% from the floor and 38.8% from 3-point range, and made the All-NBA Third Team. He signed a five-year, $244 million extension in July 2023 and will make $48,924,624 this season.

Pacers training camp opens Sept. 29. Indiana opens the regular season Oct. 21 at New Orleans, hosts Dallas on Oct. 23, and meets the champion New York Knicks on Nov. 13 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in NBA Cup play.

fullText:
You don't put up 60+ points in back-to-back games for the first time since 1915 without a total team effort. But even then some Bulldogs are bound to distinguish themselves. Those valiant warriors in Red and Black are your MVDs, the Most Valuable Dawgs from Georgia's 70-20 victory over Western Kentucky.

Offense: Gunner Stockton. There's no point in overthinking this one. Gunner finished 13 of 16 for 234 yards passing and 5 touchdowns in a shade under two quarters of work. That's downright surgical in its efficiency. If he can continue to carve up defenses that way in the SEC schedule, the Bulldog offense is heading for a big year.

Defense:Chris Cole. Like most of the Bulldog starters Cole took limited snaps, but while he was in he was all over the Hilltopper offense. Cole finished with 3 tackles, 2 of them solo stops, and got consistent pass rush pressure both inside and outside. It was a really solid, consistent effort for the physically gifted linebacker. 

Special teams: AJ Kruah. Kruah also led the team in tackles, by the way, but his forced fumble on the game's opening play set the tone for the day. On a day when Kirby Smart specifically called out his second and third teamers for not being prepared to play, Kruah absolutely came ready to work.

title: Illinois has no answer for Nate Sheppard, whose 147 rushing yards and 3 total TDs fuel Duke’s 31-27 win
description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Illinois went into its game against Duke on Saturday at Gies Memorial Stadium with questions about its tackling. Nate Sheppard exacerbated the issue. fullText:
CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Illinois went into its game against Duke on Saturday at Gies Memorial Stadium with questions about its tackling.

Nate Sheppard exacerbated the issue.

The Duke running back slipped through the grasps of many Illini defenders on the way to 147 rushing yards, 41 receiving yards and three total touchdowns in the Blue Devils' 31-27 victory. Illinois left the field Saturday evening 1-1 and with issues to address in new coordinator Bobby Hauck's defense.

The Illini offense, fueled by a monster game from wide receiver Collin Dixon, tried to keep pace. But Duke took its first lead to open the third quarter, and the Illini didn't recover despite playing in front of an orange-clad crowd that was announced to be a sellout.

Sheppard was a concern entering the game.

In Duke's 17-3, season-opening win against Tulane, Sheppard rushed for 227 yards on 35 carries — 6.5 yards per carry — with two touchdowns.

Meanwhile, the Illini had defensive struggles in their 42-23 opening win against UAB.

Illinois coach Bret Bielema and Hauck — the former Montana and UNLV head coach in his first season with the Illini — both addressed the tackling problems after the win over UAB by saying they didn't do a lot of live tackling in practice in the weeks leading up to the game to avoid injuries. They both indicated they thought it would be a fixable issue.

But Sheppard had 101 rushing yards, a touchdown, 18 receiving yards and a score in the first half alone for Duke (2-0) as the Illini went into halftime clinging to a 24-21 lead.

It was more of the same after halftime, and Sheppard scored on a 3-yard touchdown catch when he avoided the tackling efforts of linebacker Robert Edmonson. That put Duke ahead 28-24, and the teams traded field goals after that.

The Illinois offense stalled in the red zone on its next drive when Katin Houser's fourth-and-2 pass to Dixon fell incomplete.

After the Illini defense forced Duke to go three-and-out, Duke cornerback Evan Smith intercepted Houser. The Blue Devils got the ball at the Illini 45-yard line but couldn't advance. Duke quarterback Walker Eget was injured on the drive and had to be helped off the field, and backup Dan Mahan threw incomplete on third down. The Illini received another chance.

But after three straight rushing plays, another Houser pass to Dixon fell incomplete on fourth-and-4. Duke went for it on fourth-and-1 to extend its final drive and pull of the victory.

Houser, in his second game since transferring in from East Carolina, completed 24 of 35 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns. Much of his production in the first half was to Dixon.

The 6-foot-1, 215-pound senior had nine catches for 135 yards and three touchdowns before halftime. He opened the Illini scoring with a leaping 13-yard touchdown catch and later had a 40-yard TD catch on fourth-and-1. He made an impressive 30-yard sideline grab with cornerback Landan Callahan blanketing him on another drive and then scored on a 2-yard touchdown catch.

Dixon finished with 11 catches for 166 yards and three touchdowns.

Eget completed 15 of 21 passes for 206 yards and three touchdowns.

The Illinois offense made it look easy on its first drive of the game. Houser completed all five of his passes for 55 yards, including the 13-yard touchdown to Dixon.

Duke responded with a touchdown drive of its own, helped by Illini holding and face-mask penalties. Sheppard also had a 30-yard run on the drive, and Eget hit Jonah Burton with a 12-yard touchdown pass to tie it 7-7.

Illini kicker Ethan Moczulski made a 51-yard field goal for a 10-7 lead with 3:41 to play in the first quarter.

On fourth-and-1 on its next drive, Illinois pulled ahead 17-7 when Dixon crossed the field past three defenders and caught a 40-yard pass from Houser.

Duke responded with some trickery, running a fake punt on third-and-2 that resulted in a 15-yard Sheppard gain. Sheppard later gained 19 yards on a play with three Illini missed tackles and scored on a 2-yard touchdown run to cut Illinois' lead to 17-14.

Dixon and Houser connected on a 30-yard catch and 2-yard touchdown on the ensuing Illini drive for a 24-14 lead, but Duke responded again, scoring on a 7-yard Sheppard touchdown catch to cut its deficit to 24-21 going into halftime.

Illinois was playing with a revamped offensive line in the game.

Right guard Brandon Henderson was knocked out of the opener against UAB with an injury, and Bielema said in advance that he would be out against Duke. Left guard Maika Matelau then wasn't dressed for the game.

Right guard TJ McMillen and left guard Brandon Hansen started in their places. McMillen left the game with an injury in the fourth quarter, and Dezmond Schuster entered in his place.

This was a different game for the Illini than last season.

Illinois beat Duke 45-19 in 2025 when the Blue Devils committed five turnovers. That Duke team was led by quarterback Darian Mensah, who controversially transferred to Miami in January. Duke then brought in Eget from San Jose State.

title: Blue Jays, Yankees Get Strong Free Agent Take on Mets’ Bo Bichette
description: New York Mets‘ Bo Bichette has a decision to make this offseason. He can forgo the $42 million per season he’s owed over the next two seasons ($84 million total) and opt out to become a free agent. Bichette has been batting .263 with 152 hits, 16 home runs, 73 RBIs, and 72 runs scored […] The post Blue Jays, Yankees Get Strong Free Agent Take on Mets’ Bo Bichette appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
New York Mets' Bo Bichette has a decision to make this offseason. He can forgo the $42 million per season he's owed over the next two seasons ($84 million total) and opt out to become a free agent.

Bichette has been batting .263 with 152 hits, 16 home runs, 73 RBIs, and 72 runs scored in 146 games this season, per StatMuse. Nonetheless, the 28-year-old has been hitting .293 with 100 hits, 11 home runs, 45 RBIs, and 44 runs scored in 87 games for the Mets since June 1, per StatMuse.

With the Mets' 2026 season winding down and the team heading toward missing the playoffs for a second straight season, Patrick McAvoy of Fastball on SI believes Bichette will have suitors this offseason, including the New York Yankees and Toronto Blue Jays.

Starting with the Yankees, if Bichette wants to remain in New York, McAvoy sees a potential there in the Bronx.

"The New York Yankees are contenders right now, but they have some questions in the infield beyond the 2026 season. Jazz Chisholm Jr. will be a free agent," McAvoy wrote in a Sept. 11 article.

"George Lombard Jr. likely will be at shortstop. But what about third base? Ryan McMahon has one more season on his deal, but is batting .214. Bichette could help New York either at second base — if Chisholm leaves — or third base."

After a challenging start to the season, Bichette settled into New York. Would he really want to start over in a new city after finally getting comfortable in the Big Apple?

If Bichette does decide that New York isn't for him, McAvoy notes that a return to the Toronto Blue Jays would be ideal. Bichette hit .294 with 904 hits, 111 home runs, 437 RBIs, and 438 runs scored in 748 games during his time in Toronto, per StatMuse.

"The Blue Jays' lineup has been brutal so far this season," McAvoy added in his article. "In fact, the Blue Jays have been a disappointment in general after making it all the way to Game 7 of the World Series last year. Bichette struggled early on this year, but he's slashing .265/.317/.399 with a .716 OPS now, along with 16 homers and 73 RBIs in 144 games played.

"The 28-year-old turned his season around and would immediately make the Blue Jays' lineup better. Plus, these two sides certainly are familiar with one another after Bichette spent the first seven seasons of his career in Toronto. If Bichette opts out, a reunion makes too much sense."

Meanwhile, John Harper of SNY believes that Bichette should look to opt in, given that the infielder might not get $42 million per year over the next two years that are still left on his contract, per Spotrac. He could earn more than the $84 million remaining on his current deal, but he would need to sign a longer contract to do so.

"You've got the lockout coming," Harper said in a Sept. 11 video on SNY's YouTube channel. "You're not sure what the salary structure is going to look like, if there's a cap or not. I think that's part of it too. [Bichette] has been good since the terrible start, but I was looking at it, and he's not a superstar. He's a really good offensive player [and] has got an under .800 OPS in the second half, when he's done most of his best hitting.

"He doesn't hit for a lot of power [and] he's been a clutch guy again since the bad start, hitting almost .300 with runners in scoring position. To me, [$84 million] for the next two years; you can go out in the market after that [but] you're not getting [$42 million] a year anymore. Now you're getting a longer contract, but I would stick it out for these two years and then maybe take my chance."

title: Michael McDowell Addresses Denny Hamlin Darlington Incident
description: Michael McDowell broke his silence on the on-track incident at Darlington involving Denny Hamlin.
fullText:
Michael McDowell broke his silence on the on-track contact between himself and NASCAR Cup Series points leader Denny Hamlin at Darlington. At the beginning of the final stage, McDowell's No. 71 car made contact with Hamlin's No. 11 machine, causing the latter to smack the outside wall.

The contact was disastrous for Hamlin as his car suffered toe link damage, forcing his No. 11 crew to make repairs. Hamlin would go a lap down but salvaged an 18th-place finish.

Hamlin's finished cost him in the points standings. The Joe Gibbs Racing driver entered Gateway with a 25-point lead. However, with his struggles coupled with Christopher Bell's victory in the Cook Out Southern 500 at Darlington, Hamlin now clings to a seven-point lead over Bell.

During media availability on Saturday at World Wide Technology Raceway, McDowell gave his side of the story.

"When he cleared up, it kinda caught me off guard but the 48 [Alex Bowman] was underneath both of us. I was trying to time getting going down the straightaway so we didn't lose two spots right when he checked up. I don't know if he just got a bad angle or because he did it so late but he lifted so much at the exit when we were almost straight that I just didn't have enough time to check out of it," McDowell said.

McDowell believes the blame rests on both he and Hamlin for the incident. Regardless, the Spire Motorsports driver did not want to be a part of it.

"The last thing you want to do is be in the story. That's not it at all. It's just unfortunate. Going back and seeing it, I think I could've done a little better, he could've done a little better and the whole thing would have been avoided, but it just happened," McDowell said.

McDowell did not qualify for the 2026 Cup Series Chase.

Because of that, the 2021 Daytona 500 winner did not want to cause any problems for any Chase drivers. When the contact between the two happened, McDowell was left stunned. Since having a look at the replay, McDowell understands how it occurred.

"When you're not in the Chase, the last thing you want to do is affect the Chase and so it's not fun. More than anything, I was shocked at first. After I watched it, it made more sense a little bit, but at first I was like, 'Man, why'd he come up at all? He didn't need to,' and then when I watched it back, I'm like, 'Oh, he probably he was clear and is just going to take the line,'" McDowell said.

McDowell has two career NASCAR Cup Series wins. His latest victory came at the Indianapolis road course in 2023.

title: Where does OU go from here after disappointing loss to Michigan?
description: Where should the Oklahoma Sooners turn after a dreadful loss to the Michigan Wolverines?
fullText:
The Oklahoma Sooners dropped to 1-1 in the 2026 season after a 17-10 loss on the road against the Michigan Wolverines. OU failed their first test of the season and played poor, sloppy football in a bad loss.

Expectations were sky-high entering the season, but just two games into Year 5 under head coach Brent Venables, the Sooners saw their season crumble in Ann Arbor. All of the offseason talk and hype that surrounded Oklahoma fell flat in the Big House.

Firstly, though the defense was much better in the second half, the Sooners did not look like a Venables-led defense in the first half. After riding the defense to 10 wins and a spot in the College Football Playoff last season, this year's defense isn't nearly as good, at least not yet. In addition to a loss on their record, the OU defense will also be without their heart and soul for a large chunk of time, as linebacker Kip Lewis was injured in the loss.

Despite only giving up 17 total points, Oklahoma's defense tackled poorly, didn't force any turnovers, and was outflanked often in the first half. The second half was far better on that side of the ball, but the Sooners still lost because of their anemic offense.

All offseason, the Sooners talked about being better at running the ball and more committed to it. That lasted one game, as Oklahoma actually looked worse on offense on Saturday than they did last year. They abandoned the running backs in the running game, and the multiple-look structure-wise largely went out the window.

All offseason long, the Sooners lauded their offensive line, which was experienced coming into the year. Against Michigan, they were dominated up front and couldn't protect the passer or open running lanes. Even though Michael Fasusi was out, OU had still expected to play a lot better than that in the trenches.

All offseason long, the Sooners talked up their new weapons in the passing game. Aside from tight end Rocky Beers, just about everyone struggled to get open against the Wolverine secondary.

All offseason long, the Sooners praised the growth of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and his ability to adapt and keep defenses guessing. On Saturday, Sooner Nation saw very little of that, as the offense Arbuckle was hired to fix still isn't close to good enough.

All offseason long, the Sooners glowed about how much better quarterback John Mateer was going to be. His hand was healthy, he watched film with Venables, he trained with Sam Bradford, he talked with Terry Bradshaw, and he got even more ripped. His improvement was a foregone conclusion, and Oklahoma bet big on him. Two games in, Mateer looks like the same player he was for the last two months of last season. He's a great athlete, but his pocket presence, accuracy, footwork, and decision-making were all well below what they needed to be to get the win on Saturday. With multiple chances to lead OU to a game-tying drive, he was not good.

All offseason long, the Sooners assured that Mateer could take them where they needed to go. Oklahoma did their best this offseason to take the pressure off of him and surround him with good weapons and a better rushing attack. However, in just the second game, OU was right back where they were last year, relying on Mateer to do everything.

Of course, it's still very early in the season, and the Sooners will have multiple opportunities to get back on playoff track with the difficult schedule they face. However, the flip side is that Oklahoma's season could go off the rails quickly if they don't improve soon, given the difficult schedule they face. Both Georgia and Texas are on the horizon, along with a gauntlet of an SEC schedule after that.

Venables signed a contract extension right before the season, and some will once again begin to question his capability to take the Sooners to the promised land, and rightfully so. Saturday's performance was not good enough. Michigan was the better, hungrier, and more desperate team, and considering the expectations OU had coming into the season, this loss dampens a lot of the excitement surrounding the 2026 Sooners. The one advantage Venables, Arbuckle, Mateer, and the rest of the team have is time to fix it this season. However, that time is running out, and Oklahoma has now played themselves into a perilous situation just two games into what was once a very promising season.

title: New Delhi weather forecast for India vs. Afghanistan: Chances of rain, average temperature for IND vs. AFG 1st T20I
description: Here's a look at what weather India and Afghanistan might expect from Delhi as they get ready to face off against each other in the Arun Jailtey stadium on Sunday.
fullText:
India will aim to start their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan on a positive note as the two sides clash at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Sunday, September 13.

Shreyas Iyer's side heads into the series aiming to build momentum ahead of a busy stretch that includes the Asian Games and a tour of New Zealand, with the squad just recovering from a string of crippling injuries to their bowling unit.

Meanwhile, Ibrahim Zadran's Afghanistan arrives as the official hosts of the series after safety issues in their home country caused the venue to be changed to New Delhi.

title: Will Mohsin Naqvi attend India vs Sri Lanka Women's Asia Cup final? Explaining potential for another trophy controversy
description: Will Mohsin Naqvi attend the Women's Asia Cup final? Explaining the potential trophy presentation controversy if India beats Sri Lanka in the Dubai title clash.
fullText:
Will Mohsin Naqvi attend India vs Sri Lanka Women's Asia Cup final? Explaining potential for another trophy controversy originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

PCB chairman and ACC president Mohsin Naqvi is set to attend the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai as chief guest.

His presence raises the prospect of another trophy controversy if India win, following the unresolved Men's Asia Cup trophy standoff in 2025.

India have already qualified for the finals unbeaten, including a seven-wicket demolition of Pakistan, who were bowled out for 55.

The Asia Cup trophy controversy that gripped cricket last year hasn't gone away, and it could potentially resurface, with Mohsin Naqvi, the PCB chairman and Asian Cricket Council president, confirmed as the expected chief guest at the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai on September 13.

When India beat Pakistan in the Men's Asia Cup final on September 28, 2025, what should have been a celebration turned into one of the most unusual scenes in tournament cricket.

MORE: Report: Another India-Naqvi trophy standoff on cards at Women's Asia Cup final

The post-match presentation was delayed by over an hour while discussions took place around who would present the trophy. Ultimately, India's players chose not to accept the silverware from Naqvi.

The squad celebrated on the podium, Naqvi left the stadium with the trophy still in hand, and it hasn't been handed over to India since. It's reportedly still sitting at the ACC office in Dubai.

The tournament had been held in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack, and Naqvi had also posted anti-India content on social media in his capacity as Pakistan's Interior Minister during the course of the event.

That combination of factors made the trophy moment explosive, and it was widely discussed for weeks after.

MORE: India women vs Bangladesh women's Asia Cup 2026 semi-final result, highlights as Shafali Verma stars in Dubai

As the ACC president, Naqvi holds the natural role of trophy presenter at continental cricket events. The Women's Asia Cup is an ACC-run tournament, which means his position gives him the right to hand over the silverware to the winning captain.

If India wins, the same question about whether to accept the trophy from him could land squarely in front of Harmanpreet Kaur's team.

The BCCI has not issued any statement about what India's women's side would do if the situation arose. That silence may be deliberate as there's little to gain from escalating the tension before the final has even been played.

India arrived at this tournament as favourites and have played like it. They've gone through the group stage without dropping a match, and beat Bangladesh in the semi-finals to seal a berth in he summit clash.

MORE: Fans react as members of Pakistan women's cricket team spotted wearing Kohli's One8 shoes

A year after the Men's Asia Cup trophy was left sitting in a Dubai office rather than with the team that won the tournament, the same circumstances are being allowed to recreate themselves.

That's a failure of administration, not just politics. The ACC has had twelve months to find a way to resolve a situation that embarrassed international cricket, and apparently nothing has been done.

Allowing the same person, in the same dual roles, to be placed in the same position at the same type of event, without any protocol in place to prevent a repeat controversy, is a choice. It's a choice that prioritises optics over resolution and leaves both the trophy and the problem still unaddressed.

title: Elena Rybakina admits she’s been suffering with ‘chronic’ fitness issue for years just after winning the US Open
description: Elena Rybakina defeated Aryna Sabalenka, 6-4, 5-7, 6-2, in the 2026 US Open final. The 27-year-old is now a three-time major champion, adding to her...
fullText:
Elena Rybakina defeated Aryna Sabalenka, 6-4, 5-7, 6-2, in the 2026 US Open final.

The 27-year-old is now a three-time major champion, adding to her 2022 Wimbledon and 2026 Australian Open wins.

Watching her lift the trophy, it is easy to forget the fitness worries that surrounded Rybakina just a few weeks ago.

She has now issued a fresh fitness update, commenting on the foot issue that forced her to retire from the Cincinnati Open quarter-finals 23 days ago.

During an interview with ESPN, Rybakina said the following.

"Honestly, my foot issue has been for years. It is kind of chronic," she said.

"It was coming on and off, but on that tournament right before the US Open, I did one movement, and it was very difficult.

"The days before, it was raining, so I was going on and off the court, and I hurt myself. We all got upset as a team.

"We started to call the doctor, and one actually helped me quite a lot. She was on the phone every day, and she was in Australia."

Rybakina only had four days of practice before the US Open, but she made them count!

"It was so difficult to manage all these things. I was not touching my racket for seven days before the tournament," she said.

"It was likely that I was going to play on Tuesday, so I got these extra days. It was just four days of practice.

"A lot of belief in yourself and talking to the team about the tactics. How I played in Canada and Cincinnati, and everything went my way. I am shocked."

Rybakina doesn't seem to think there is a permanent solution to her foot problem.

But if she can play like this with a chronic injury, then that is probably good news for the rest of the WTA Tour!

Rybakina is now a three-time major champion.

That moves her into sixth on the list of active Grand Slam women's singles champions.

Multiple Grand Slam women's singles champions (active)

If she wins the next Grand Slam event, the 2027 Australian Open, Rybakina will tie Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka on four majors.

The Kazakhstani could then set her sights on Iga Swiatek (6) and Venus Williams (7).

Rybakina won't want to get ahead of herself, though, and knows just how difficult it is to win Grand Slams.

After winning her maiden major title at Wimbledon in 2022, Rybakina failed to win any of her next 13 Grand Slam events.

With young players emerging like Alex Eala, Iva Jovic, and Victoria Mboko, Rybakina must capitalise on her career-best form and win as many majors as she can, while she can.

Only time will tell if Rybakina can add to her major tally in 2027.

Before then, she will likely attend the China Open, Wuhan Open, and the WTA Finals.

They aren't Grand Slams, but they are 'big tournaments' that Rybakina will want to win.

The 2026 China Open begins on Monday, September 28.

title: Why a certain WWE-style belt means Alabama football defense is at its best
description: After Luke Metz did his job, the Alabama football linebacker got to celebrate.
fullText:
LEXINGTON, Ky. — After Luke Metz did his job, the Alabama football linebacker got to celebrate.

Trailing by a touchdown in the first quarter against Kentucky, Metz was tasked with reading quarterback Kenny Minchey. Once Minchey threw, Metz stepped in front of the receiver, snagged the ball and ran it 34 yards for a touchdown.

From there, Metz got a chance to participate in a tradition Alabama has continued for years into this new Crimson Tide era: a WWE-style belt that celebrates takeaways. Once Metz got ahold of it, he called it "surreal."

"You want to get a picture with the belt," Metz said. "That's the goal."

When Alabama's defense is at its best, that "turnover belt" is being passed around. And in Saturday's 45-17 win against the Wildcats, the belt had its share of wearers with three forced turnovers: an interception and two fumble recoveries.

But Alabama doesn't need a belt or any evidence of a job well done. To linebacker Caleb Woodson, takeaways or crazy stat lines is just evidence of Kane Wommack's plan coming to fruition.

"Swarm D is going to the ball every play," Woodson said. "Whenever 11 bodies are out on the field, 11 bodies (are) getting to the ball, trying to affect the game."

Along with three turnovers, Alabama's defense allowed just 10 points and 209 yards. In the second half, Kentucky had 62 yards, three first downs and no points.

Through two games, Alabama's defense has allowed 20 points. Opposing offenses have converted one third down on 23 tries.

"Our defense did a good job of continuing to evolve throughout the game," Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said, "but I thought we had a pretty good plan, a pretty good handle on things from the get go."

To defensive lineman Devan Thompkins, that success stems from trust of Wommack's calls and trust that his teammates are all in step with one another.

"We just went out and played our brand of football," Thompkins said. "That's what got us to where we were."

title: Arch Manning’s Parents & Family Have Unique Ties to Peyton & Eli Manning
description: Yes, Arch Manning is related to Peyton and Eli Manning. Learn more about Manning's parents, Cooper and Ellen, as well as his famous family. The post Arch Manning’s Parents & Family Have Unique Ties to Peyton & Eli Manning appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
When it comes to football, it is hard to find a more recognizable last name than Manning, and Arch Manning is just the latest in a long line of quarterbacks in the family. Arch's parents, Cooper Manning and Ellen Heidingsfelder, can often be seen at Texas games cheering on their son.

Cooper's brothers are NFL legends, Peyton and Eli Manning, but Arch's dad also spent time playing football. While he did not have an NFL career, Cooper played college football at Ole Miss.

Arch's father dabbled in the media space while his brothers played in the NFL, and Cooper also works in the finance industry. Peyton and Eli are Arch's uncles, a good resource to have when you are the Texas starting quarterback.

Arch's grandfather, Archie Manning, also played in the NFL after having a standout college career at Ole Miss.

Here's what you need to know about the Manning family.

Arch's mom, Ellen, was also an athlete as part of the New Orleans' Academy of the Sacred Heart's volleyball team that made it to the state championship. While most of the Manning family is known for football, Ellen built a successful career as a lawyer.

Arch's mom got candid about some of the challenges Arch has with fame.

"He struggles with that right now," Ellen told The Athletic's Bruce Feldman during a June 25, 2025, feature titled, "Raising Arch: How Cooper and Ellen prepared Texas' QB for the Manning family spotlight."

"Especially when he's in Austin, he feels like he can't go out because everybody wants to take a picture. He said it's not even the ones that are coming up and saying, 'Hey, can I get a picture?' Ellen added.

"He's always been very gracious about that. He learned that from his grandfather. You always take the time to take a picture, talk to a fan."

Like other star college quarterbacks, Arch has been part of the Manning Passing Academy, a notable camp where the top collegiate signal-callers work with the best high school QBs. Arch had no problem staying at the dorm just like everyone else when he was attending the camp.

"In his early teens at the annual Manning Passing Academy, he'd choose staying in dorms with friends and pizza over going to meetings with college quarterbacks," ESPN's Chuck Culpepper detailed in a September 11, story titled, "How Arch Manning handles formidable fame."

As for advice from his famous uncles, Arch revealed that Peyton and Eli encourage him to enjoy college instead of worrying about the NFL.

"Yeah, a lot of advice," Arch explained to People's Skyler Caruso during a September 5, story.

"They ultimately just told me to enjoy college right now, worry about that when the time comes, just take it day by day and try to be a good guy."

title: Kahleah Copper wants to play with joy
description: LOS ANGELES -- The Phoenix Mercury visited the Los Angeles Sparks last month at the Galen Center in the University of Southern California.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES -- The Phoenix Mercury visited the Los Angeles Sparks last month at the Galen Center in the University of Southern California. A lot changed from their visit before that a couple of weeks before to their game at USC.

For Kahleah Copper, a lot changed for her as well. Hours after their game against the Sparks on July 22nd, Copper was named to the All-Star team as she replaced her friend, then-Sparks guard Kelsey Plum.

About a week after All-Star weekend, Plum was traded to the Mercury and the friends were suddenly teammates.

"(Plum brought) her energy, her vibes, her leadership, her championship experience (to the team)," Copper said before their game against the Sparks at USC. "She knows what it takes to win. I'm glad to play alongside with her."

As for All-Star Weekend after expecting to get some rest?

"It was cool. It was a good experience," Copper said about that weekend. "There were a lot of good people."

The Mercury are out of the playoff chase but Copper still wants to build momentum towards the end of their season.

"I think we've got to play with some joy," Copper said about the rest of the campaign. "We've got to compete harder and play with joy. Just have that toughness, play with that energy."

While this W season won't end with a title for Copper, she's part of Team USA, who is playing in the gold medal round on Sunday. She scored nine of her 13 points in that all-important second half against Spain in the semifinal round. At the very least, Copper is making winning plays in the international stage. She's averaging 7.8 points and 4.4 rebounds in five games of the World Cup.

Not only does she get joy in playing but there's joy on the men's stage, too. LeBron James signed with the Sixers in free agency and Copper, a Philly girl, was very happy about that result.

"I'm excited that he's in the city," Copper beamed. "I'm excited to see the Sixers win and try to compete in the championship. Let's not forget about Jaylen Brown. I'm super excited to see that team come together. I'm planning on being courtside."

And America is planning on being courtside for Copper and a possible gold medal from the FIBA World Cup on Sunday as they try to defeat France for all the marbles.

title: Ohio State vs. Texas three and out halftime review | Buckeyes Wire
description: It's halftime in Austin, Texas, and here's three things that we took from Ohio State vs. Texas through the first 30 minutes of play.
fullText:
It's halftime in Austin with Ohio State and Texas engaging in one of the most anticipated nonconference games of the college football season. The Buckeyes used some Longhorn mistakes and some excellent play on both sides of the ball to take a 20-3 lead into the locker room, which is banking the national narrative in this one.

We like to look back on the first half and take three observations and takeaways from what we saw through the first 30 minutes of action, and in this case, there's plenty to talk about. Here are three observations from what we saw from the Buckeyes and Longhorns in the first half of what should be one whale of a second half to finish this thing out.

Ohio State forces a fumble against Texas on the first play of the game😤

(via ESPN) pic.twitter.com/kxvE7F9D0B

The defense hasn't been very stingy in stopping the run through the middle, but it has been very opportunistic in forcing two turnovers. Both of them led to two scores and have really been the difference in the game so far. You have to think that the turnovers aren't going to continue, so Ohio State will have to continue to make plays while getting equal possessions.

Jeremiah Smith: Freakshow

(Via: ABC)pic.twitter.com/jQuJSiQ1A4

A lot of the talk coming into this game was the ability of Texas to limit Smith the last two times these teams matched up. So far, that hasn't been the case in this one. Jeremiah Smith had six catches for 110 yards and a touchdown in the first half and is a big part of the game plan.

Offensive coordinator Arthur Smith is doing a great job of moving him around and creating mismatches, and the Texas defense has really had no answer for it. We'll see if there are halftime adjustments made because if Julian Sayin continues to find Smith, it's hard to think the Longhorns can pull this one out.

ARCH MANNING WITH A BULLET BUT RYAN WINGO DROPS IT.....pic.twitter.com/JvDidKva62

Texas has not played good football, and that's the reason this game is in Ohio State's favor. We already talked about the two turnovers, but there have been a couple of dropped passes, missed assignments on defense, and Arch Manning has misfired on some key throws.

Don't expect that to continue, and it feels like the Buckeyes should be up by more. Let's hope the defense continues to play well and that the offense can finish off drives because this one feels like it's going to tighten up.

title: Rams Defensive Coordinator Under Fire After Disappointing Start
description: The Los Angeles Rams were massively disappointing on both ends of the field, culminating in a 27-7 loss to the San Fransico 49ers. The post Rams Defensive Coordinator Under Fire After Disappointing Start appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams were massively disappointing on both ends of the field, culminating in a 27-7 loss to the San Fransico 49ers.

However, given all of the additions to the defense, that was the side with the higher expectations.

Aaron Donald returned, albeit not for Week 1, while the best defensive player in the sport, Myles Garrett, was added via trade, along with two good cornerbacks in Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie.

In 2025, this unit was already one of the better groups in the league, and with so many upgrades, it was expected to be a super unit.

The Rams allowed 27 points and had only a 5.6% pressure rate, dwarfed by the 49ers' 27.6% rate. The Niners totaled 379 yards and 5.9 yards per play as well.

On third down, SF converted seven of 12 scenarios. The Rams allowed more explosive plays, and they had no answers in the run game.

After the Rams' loss, ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky said the defense was a bigger concern than the offense, specifically calling out Los Angeles defensive coordinator Chris Shula.

"I am very concerned about that defense, and I'm very concerned about their defensive coordinator," Orlovsky said on ESPN's "Get Up!" 

"The last four games that we have watched this defense on the field with all kinds of talent, they have stunk. Bryce Young lit them up. Caleb Williams lit them up. Sam Darnold lit them up. Brock Purdy lit them up."

While Orlovsky is right that the Rams have disappointed in some marquee games defensively, this season is only one game old, and much more is to come from Shula.

The team stayed in heavy zone coverage rather than mixing in much man, which let the 49ers gash them.

The defensive scheme looked quite vanilla for the Rams overall, and they are known for hiding things they'll do throughout the season early on.

All eyes will be on what adjustments they make once Donald enters the mix and Donald gets healthy.

title: US Open champ Rybakina on top of world after injury scare
description: Elena Rybakina is on top of the tennis world, celebrating her first US Open title and her rise to number one barely more than three weeks after she feared injury would force her out of the final Grand Slam of the year.Kazakhstan's Rybakina beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday to claim her third Grand Slam title.
fullText:
Elena Rybakina is on top of the tennis world, celebrating her first US Open title and her rise to number one barely more than three weeks after she feared injury would force her out of the final Grand Slam of the year.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday to claim her third Grand Slam title.

She'd already assured herself of toppling Sabalenka from the number one spot just by reaching the semi-finals.

"I can't find words right now, honestly," Rybakina said. "I don't expect nothing like this coming to this tournament. I've been dealing with a little bit with an injury, but somehow everything aligned together on my side."

The "little bit of an injury" saw Rybakina hobble out of her Cincinnati quarter-final on August 20 -- 10 days before the start of the US Open -- unable to put weight on her left heel.

"It wasn't the best time, for sure, because I was so upset," Rybakina said. "I didn't know actually how it's going to be day by day.

"We arrive to New York. We did MRI. It didn't look that great. We had to talk with a lot of doctors to get opinion what we should do."

With a doctor in Australia providing valuable long-distance advice, Rybakina and her team came up with a plan to manage her training, rest and treatment and give her a chance at her second major title of the year, after her victory over Sabalenka at the Australian Open.

Her run to the final included an impressive fourth-round victory over two-time champion Naomi Osaka before come-from-behind wins over resurgent Olympic gold medallist Zheng Qinwen and former champion Coco Gauff.

It all led to her 18th showdown with Sabalenka in a rivalry that has emerged as the most dynamic on the WTA tour.

Having narrowed Sabalenka's lead in their head to 10-8, Rybakina is looking forward to more chances to take on her fiery rival, whose on-court personality is the perfect foil to her own cool approach.

"I don't know what the future will bring, but it's always very difficult matches against Aryna," she said. "I feel like we push each other to be better after such tough battles."

The two seem destined to tussle for the top spot for some time. But other players -- Gauff and Jessica Pegula -- also had a chance to seize the number one ranking in New York, so Rybakina knows that Sabalenka is not the only rival she must be wary of.

"I feel like not only with her, with also other players, top players, you always want to try something new, to change in your game, to be better," she said.

"I don't know what future is going to bring, but I hope success and some more wins."

title: MSU ground game wakes up, runs over Eastern Michigan after halftime
description: Cam Edwards rushed for 152 yards and two touchdowns in a 35-7 win over Eastern Michigan.
fullText:
EAST LANSING — Ten yards from the end zone, Michigan State running back Cam Edwards strained as three defenders tried to wrangle him to the ground in the backfield. He dove forward toward the line of scrimmage with seemingly all his might. It wound up costing him. For the first time in Edwards' five-year college career, he fumbled.

If that fumble pierced Edwards' perfection protecting the football, then he made up for it the next play: a 40-yard gain that set up the final touchdown of Michigan State's 35-7 win over Eastern Michigan at Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 12. He finished the game with 21 carries for 152 yards and two scores. Both are season highs, two games into his Spartan career.

"It's not acceptable," Edwards said of the fumble. "I was beating myself up about it, but I think I did a really good way of responding for the team and just putting that play aside."

In a game MSU only led 14-7 at halftime, both outgained and out-possessed by a Mid-American Conference team it entered a 17½-point favorite against, Michigan State turned to its run game to lead it forward. It ran for 198 yards in the second half, and 258 of its 472 total yards in the entire game.

All those rushing yards offered redemption for an offense that prides itself on running the football. And for Edwards, who prides himself on protecting it.

"We didn't want his last touch to be what happened there," MSU coach Pat Fitzgerald said.

Three of Michigan State's five touchdowns came on the ground, two of those direct snaps to Edwards. He rushed in a 1-yard touchdown to take a 14-0 lead midway through the second quarter and added a 2-yard gain in the third.

"When I was in high school, I used to play a little bit of quarterback, and we used to do a little bit of wildcat," Edwards said of the genesis of those looks. "So you know, I kind of just stretched it over to Coach (Nick) Sheridan, and was just making a joke out of it. And then he actually took it really serious."

So did Eastern Michigan. Michigan State called 45 runs to 26 passing plays. However, the Spartans had only mustered 60 yards rushing by halftime compared to 107 by the Eagles. In the second half, Eastern Michigan saw more of the team it expected to see: one that feeds itself through its gifted tailback Edwards.

"I think what they want to be is downhill running, tough, physical — you know what I mean?" Eastern Michigan coach Chris Creighton said. "Big Ten, Michigan State football, right? And I think that you can see that just in the first two games."

"We took their best punch in the second quarter," Fitzgerald said. "And again, credit to Coach Creighton and the staff."

Already, Michigan State is up to 408 rushing yards through two games, with 250 of those and three touchdowns belonging to Edwards on 48 carries. Twenty-one of those carries came Saturday, and the Spartans plan on many more for the bell cow. Two of those — the aforementioned 40-yarder and a 33-yard gain in the third quarter — accounted for nearly half his yards Saturday and both led to touchdown drives.

"It makes it a lot easier on me to go out there and win a game when you got a guy like this guy running for I don't know how many it was, but I know it's a lot," quarterback Alessio Milivojevic said of Edwards. "You got Marv (Parrish), Jazz (Patterson), and the guys in front that played their butt off. So I think it just makes it easier on me, and I think together, mixing the run and pass, it makes it a tough offense to stop."

More: Cam Edwards aims to be 'best running back in the country' for Spartans

All three of those touchdowns, surprisingly, have come on direct snaps. If Michigan State is skipping the middle man on some looks, Milivojevic hopes his running back doesn't get too carried away.

"This guy thinks he's a quarterback, but I think he's a pretty good running back," Milivojevic joked. "So hopefully he can stay in that position."

title: Maryland volleyball takes down Princeton, 3-0, for 6th win of 2026
description: The victory marked the Terps’ fourth succesive straight set victory for the first time since 2023.
fullText:
Sydney Bryant was the spark behind Maryland volleyball's offensive momentum, leading an attack that overwhelmed Princeton throughout Saturday night's match.

The Terps came out on top in straight sets and are now 6-1 to begin the season, their best start since 2021. Head coach Adam Hughes had high praise for Maryland's confidence in the locker room and on the court this year.

"I'll give a lot of the shoutout to the seniors. In the beginning of the year, we talked about how freshmen were going to be a big factor and how the seniors are going to have to be big leaders and be composed, and they've done that. It's been at practice, it's been at meetings, it's been across the board — not just how we perform in matches," Hughes said.

Maryland shot out to an early lead, kicked off by a kill from Melby that was followed by a service ace from Brooklynne Brass. Two service errors later placed Princeton in a 5-1 deficit to begin the match.

Duru Gökçen and Eva Rohrbach posed a threatening blocking duo at the net in the first set and anchored an effective defensive unit that halted multiple attacks from the Tigers. Their blocking led to a kill from Sara Toth that forced Princeton to call a timeout as the Terps took a 9-3 lead.

Rohrbach came out of the timeout with a kill, giving the Terps more energy to ride off of. Veteran outside hitter Bryant led by example with three crucial kills. They, along with a kill and service ace from Melby and a kill from Rohrbach, allowed Maryland to take an 11-point lead, their largest of the set.

Princeton attempted to make a late surge and steal the set, cutting the lead to as little as six with a kill from Erin McNair. However, a late push from Princeton was not enough to stifle the Terps' momentum. Errors by the Tigers and Maryland's aggressive defense allowed the Terps to close out the first set, 25-17.

The second set had a more balanced start in comparison to the opening set. Gameplay was back-and-forth for the first few points. Toth assisted on three kills – two from Melby, and one from Rohrbach – to spark a 3-0 run that allowed the Terps to briefly pull away from the stalemate that characterized the start of the set.

Maryland couldn't yet fully break away as it did in the first set, though. Tigers outside hitter Sarah Hom cutMaryland's lead to two points. Unfortunately for Princeton, the pause in the Terps' momentum wouldn't last for long. With a kill from Gökçen and Raina Chwialkowski recording a series of points through service and errors by the Tigers, the Terps went on an 8-2 run.

Princeton wouldn't recover from the deficit the run caused. Bryant added three kills to her impressive total late in the set that allowed Maryland to pull away. Ashtyn Syms attempted to spark some momentum for Princeton with a kill to fend off a set point by Maryland. However, Melby secured her eighth kill of the game as Maryland secured its second-set win, 25-15.

The Tigers took their first lead of the match with two kills from Clark Taylor. This would be the first and only advantage for Princeton, as Maryland was able to pull away and capitalize on the Tigers' errors. Those errors sparked a 7-1 run for the Terps, as Bryant and Gökçen added kills to increase the lead.

Action was balanced for the middle portion of the third set. Attack errors from both sides kept the Maryland lead around five points until two errors from Princeton's Ashtyn Sims landed the Terps a 20-13 lead late in the set. The Tigers fought back, with crucial kills from Taylor and McNair that brought Maryland's lead to three as Princeton attempted to steal the set from the Terps. Instead, the Tigers' hopes would fall short as two errors gave Maryland the deciding points to rise to victory in a 25-20 third set.

1. Team chemistry. Communication between Toth and Maryland's veteran outside hitters Melby and Bryant allowed the two to combine for 23 kills in an aggressive attack that was almost unstoppable. When asked about what went well offensively today, Bryant praised Toth.

"There was a lot of communication between us and our setter. She's not afraid to go back to us, and that clear line of communication really helped," Bryant said.

2. Big-time blocking. Maryland's blocking core in Gökçen and Rohrbach fended off fierce attacks from Princeton and earned crucial points for the Terps that sparked runs.

3. Attacking versatility. Hughes was able to rely on Bryant and Melby for individual point production at different moments throughout the match, allowing the veterans to rest and balance the offensive load.

title: From struggling to walk to lifting trophy - how Rybakina triumphed
description: Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.
fullText:
Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina produced a brilliant performance to beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2 in Saturday's final and repeat her Australian Open success against the same player in January.

Clutching the trophy on Saturday night, Rybakina reflected that "some magic is happening" for her after her difficult lead-in to the tournament.

The 27-year-old aggravated a foot injury during her quarter-final in Cincinnati against Iga Swiatek last month, a little over a week before the final major of the year began.

Playing on through injury could have disastrous consequences for the rest of the season - but Rybakina, knowing the top ranking was in her grasp, wanted to try and play in the final Grand Slam of the year.

"I was so upset. I didn't know actually how it was going to be day by day," she said.

"We arrived in New York and did an MRI. It didn't look that great.

"I couldn't even walk for the next few days without pain.

"I was lucky enough to have a very good doctor in Australia. She was on the phone with us all the time and somehow, with the team, we made a plan."

Rybakina did not do any on-court training for a week but daily recovery sessions in the gym - plus trips for dinner and to the cinema to "switch the mind" - helped get her ready for another major triumph.

She won her first four matches at Flushing Meadows without dropping a set, including seeing off four-time major winner Naomi Osaka.

Her run from then on - which included beating Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen in the quarter-finals, outlasting third seed Coco Gauff in the semis and outplaying top seed Sabalenka in the final - was nothing short of outstanding.

"I was so unlucky with the injury, but I'm very proud," Rybakina said.

Listen: US Open podcast - Rybakina crowned champion

American Shelton to face Zverev in US Open final

Rybakina had already been confirmed as world number one by reaching the semi-finals in New York. The fact that her final opponent was Sabalenka, the player she will replace at the top of the rankings, added an extra dimension to Saturday's championship match.

Rybakina won the first set despite her serve, one of her biggest weapons, misfiring.

She landed only 27% of her first serves during the opener, but still won 22 of 30 points behind her serve and did not face a break point as she took the lead.

Sabalenka eventually broke in the 12th game of the second set to send their match the distance, but Rybakina who dominated the decider.

While the Belarusian grew visibly more frustrated as the final slipped away, Rybakina remained remarkably composed.

"The way she [Rybakina] quietly walks around, she doesn't really lift her head up and she gives no emotion away whatsoever," former British number one Annabel Croft said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"Rybakina is like a machine out there. You never know what's going on in her head."

However, nerves did show when Rybakina threw in two double faults as she served for the title.

At 40-30, the trophy in her sights, Rybakina could have blinked. Instead, she cooly sent down her 12th ace of the match to secure her third Grand Slam title.

The second seed produced her biggest celebration of her three major wins - a smile and both arms raised in celebration as she took in the applause.

Rybakina has now won two of her three Grand Slam finals against Sabalenka, all of which have come on their favoured hard courts.

On Monday, Rybakina will become the 30th different women to top the world rankings.

She is a different personality to Sabalenka, who held the position for the past 99 weeks, but Croft believes she will "take it in her stride".

"I actually think she has the right personality to deal with it," Croft said.

"There are going to be a lot of players around her nipping at her heels. She can fluctuate with her levels, but when it really matters, we've seen her be able to bring it to the table.

"It's not going to be easy to hang onto it. I think women's tennis is really exciting right now."

Rybakina has completed three parts of the career Grand Slam, with just a French Open victory missing from her collection.

After winning Wimbledon in 2022, she did not claim her second major until January's Australian Open, and has now added a third in New York.

She has never previously been further than the quarter-finals at Roland Garros, although she did win a WTA 1000 event on clay in Rome in 2023.

Former British number one Laura Robson said on Sky Sports: "She is an all-surface player - clay is the worst one, but when you get her on something that's quite lively or quick, she's unplayable at times.

"I genuinely think she will win many more Slams. I just don't see, when her serve and return are on, how pretty much anyone can beat her on a hard court."

fullText:
Elena Rybakina demonstrated why she is the best women's player in the world by beating two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka to win her first US Open title.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina already knew she would be the new world number one after Saturday's final regardless of the result, and she celebrated with a 6-4 5-7 6-2 victory over the player she will replace.

Rybakina was the more composed of the two throughout as she claimed the third Grand Slam title of her career, having triumphed at Wimbledon in 2022 and the Australian Open earlier this year.

Sabalenka hoped to soften the blow of losing the top ranking by winning a third consecutive US Open title - but looked fraught in a tense performance.

Rybakina and Sabalenka have developed a strong rivalry built not only on their outstanding talent but their contrasting personalities.

And Rybakina's ice-cool composure - the direct opposite of the Belarusian's combustible nature - was a key difference as she took control at Flushing Meadows.

Rybakina stayed calm in an opening set where her first serve let her down and, despite her biggest weapon not firing on all cylinders, was able to execute a devastating returning game which left Sabalenka frustrated.

Sabalenka's groundstrokes improved as Rybakina's level dropped slightly in a tighter second set, taking her third opportunity to force a decider when she swarmed over Rybakina's second serve in the 12th game.

But the loose shots from Sabalenka reappeared in the third set - as did the negativity.

Rybakina's deep returning pinned Sabalenka to the baseline as she broke for a 2-1 lead, which allowed the incoming world number one to grow in stature.

There was a sign of nerves when Rybakina produced a double fault on her first championship point, but she reset admirably to hammer down an ace and underline her status as the best player in the world.

From struggling to walk to lifting trophy - how Rybakina triumphed

Listen to All About US Open: Rybakina crowned champion as Sabalenka melts down

Rybakina rarely shows emotion on the court but there was a brief flash of a smile as she clinched her second major victory of an outstanding 2026 season.

That illustrated the sense of satisfaction she felt after winning a title few had predicted - not only because she had never previously gone beyond the last 16 in New York but the circumstances coming into the final major of the season.

With her penetrating serve and thunderous groundstrokes, Rybakina has a brand of first-strike tennis that can take the racquet out of anyone's hands.

Therefore it has been a surprise she has not enjoyed greater success on the Flushing Meadows hard courts, perhaps a result of her personality not being particularly suited to the brash nature of New York.

"I was coming here for the last 10 years and it was never successful. I'm falling in love with New York more and more," Rybakina, 27, said.

What makes the second seed's victory even more remarkable is that she was unsure if she would be fit enough to even play.

Rybakina was unable to walk for several days after injuring her ankle in the Cincinnati Open quarter-finals, putting her chances of competing here in serious jeopardy.

Not only was Rybakina able to play, but she cruised through her opening four matches thanks to a huge service game that rarely allowed opponents to get into points.

Rybakina's next two wins over China's Zheng Qinwen and home favourite Coco Gauff required more work after losing the first sets, proving she had the durability to come through tough battles.

Against Sabalenka, she showed both facets of her game, bullying her from the baseline and digging in when necessary to leave her only a French Open title away from the career Grand Slam.

"Some magic is happening. I was unlucky with injury and just going day by day," Rybakina told Sky Sports.

"We didn't know how it was going to be so I'm super happy and still can't believe it."

The chance to beat the woman who had taken her number one ranking was extra motivation for Sabalenka.

However, it was evident from the early stages that the stress of the situation was still troubling the four-time major singles champion - and Rybakina's superb return of serve in the early exchanges only exacerbated it.

The pressure Sabalenka was feeling manifested in some aggressive second serves, and it was unsurprising to see one go long for a double fault on the decisive break point in the opening set.

While Sabalenka showed the resilience which she has demonstrated in her ascent to the top of the sport, she never looked completely at ease.

Dramatic displays of emotion designed to let off steam - yelling, flinging her arms in the air, bouncing her racquet off the court and hiding underneath her towel - were not enough to help produce a gutsy victory which would have ranked among her best.

Instead she will have to come to terms with another near miss at a Grand Slam.

It was Sabalenka's fifth defeat from nine majors final and provides further weight to the argument that she has underachieved at the biggest tournaments given her dominance on the WTA Tour.

"The last thing I want to do right now is give a speech but I will try my best," an emotional Sabalenka told the 24,000 crowd on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I wish I could have performed a little bit better, but I guess next year."

title: MSU defense show flaws without Jordan Hall, but return imminent
description: Jordan Hall missed Michigan State football's 35-7 win over Eastern Michigan with a right elbow injury, but he could play next week at Notre Dame.
fullText:
EAST LANSING — Michigan State coach Pat Fitzgerald thinks he may have his most important defensive player back for next week's game against Notre Dame.

In his postgame press conference after a 35-7 win over Eastern Michigan on Saturday, Sept. 12, Fitzgerald said that starting middle linebacker Jordan Hall was not cleared for the game by medical personnel but could be available for Week 3's rivalry game in South Bend.

"Jordan was really close playing today," Fitzgerald said. "Medical team told us that he was not cleared here late in the week. We made that decision collectively together to make sure that we think about his health, safety, and well-being. And I expect if we practice tomorrow that he'll be ready to go."

Hall made 88 tackles last season to lead Michigan State's defense and is a two-time captain. The senior made four tackles in 25 snaps in Week 1's win over Toledo but came on and off the field with a right elbow injury sustained on the second drive of the season. He walked into Spartan Stadium on Saturday with a brace on that right arm.

MSU LB Jordan Hall with a brace on his right elbow as he takes the Spartan Walk. 

Saw him wince on a couple of handshakes. We’ll see how he looks in warmups.@detroitnews pic.twitter.com/qklOKEfVbs

Without Hall, Michigan State leaned on linebacker Brady Pretzlaff to be its green dot — the player who communicates with defensive staff with helmet comms — and played a mix of Dion Crawford, Caleb Wheatland and Cam Stodghill next to him in a number of 4-2-5 and 4-3 looks. Fitzgerald said there is work for MSU's defense to do without Hall from a communication standpoint.

Pretzlaff credited Hall with preparing him to deliver on Saturday, when his eight tackles tied safety Devin Vaught for the team lead.

"I think Jordan himself has been a great leader throughout this week," Pretzlaff said. "It's hard for a guy like that who has played so much and is so passionate about the game to go down, and he's done a great job of himself kind of taking on the coaching role and getting us ready and kind of taking that role forward. So it's been great to see that, and I think our preparation really helped us attack it today."

More: Gaylord's Brady Pretzlaff proving MSU coaches' investment was worth it

The Spartans are 29-49-1 all-time against Notre Dame, which is ranked No. 4 in the USA Today Coaches Poll. In the past seven meetings dating back to 2009, Michigan State is 2-5 with an overtime win. Having Hall back will be important for Michigan State going into South Bend.

"Jordan's a huge piece of our program. He'll go down in Spartan lore when his career is said and done," Fitzgerald said. "So I don't want to minimize not having that big of a fixture of our defense out there, but it's next-man-up mentality, and those guys that went out there, I think learned a lot throughout the course of the game. I thought they played much better in the second half, and we need to continue to reinforce those guys playing that way."

Saturday, Sept. 19's game comes 60 years after Notre Dame ran out the clock against Michigan State in 1966's "Game of the Century," a 10-10 tie that led to both teams sharing pieces of the national championship that year.

Michigan State hasn't played Notre Dame since Sept. 23, 2017, when it lost 38-18 at Spartan Stadium.

title: Bay Area charity golf event raises $5.6 million for Curry's 'Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation'
description: The 7th Annual Workday Charity Classic at Palo Alto Hills Golf and Country Club raised more than $5.6 million dollars to support Oakland students and families.
fullText:
A perfect day on the golf course, resulted in a big win for Oakland children for many years to come. The 7th Annual Workday Charity Classic at Palo Alto Hills Golf and Country Club raised more than $5.6 million dollars to support Oakland students and families. The annual golf event is the signature fundraising event for the Curry's 'Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation.'

Seven years running, the @workday Charity Classic has turned a day on the green into real support for Oakland kids. This year’s event raised more than $5.6 million to support students, made possible in part by a generous matching gift from Aneel Bhusri, co-founder of Workday. pic.twitter.com/BijN8LaoIA

"This event is our biggest fundraiser of the year and the impact it helps us unlock in Oakland is huge," said Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation CEO Chris Helfrich. "To be able to pull together 150 of our best partners and supporters for a day full of joy and golf like this it's a big deal for 'Eat. Learn. Play.' and we are very fortunate to be able to raise the money and invest it back out so that kids in Oakland get what they deserve."

Related https://abc7news.com/post/golden-state-warriors-stephen-curry-surprises-minnesota-boy-viral-range-shot-invite-game-season/19229529/

MORE: 'Christmas with the Curry's' celebrates a decade of giving back to the community

So, when you actually start to see that come to fruition and you start to see the statistics change and these kids thriving in their environment, there is nothing better than that," said Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation co-founder Ayesha Curry.

Since the summer of 2019, 'Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation' has invested more than $100 million in Oakland students and families. The foundation's focus has been to bring resources to those who need it most and making sure the pillars of food (Eat), education (Learn) and activity (Play) are met.

title: Braves crush Phillies on big fourth inning
description: The Braves all-but locked up the NL East with a romp over the Phillies on Saturday night, as Tyler Mahle cruised
fullText:
After an epic 11-inning win Friday night against the Phillies, the Braves were hoping to finish them off in the division race. They got a bit of a boost from the Phillies scratching Jesus Luzardo with long-running shoulder soreness.

Tyler Mahle cruised through the first two hitters before Bryce Harper hit a monster homer and took a comical amount of time rounding the bases, clearly hitting back at the controversy from Zach Wheeler's comments about Ronald Acuna's home run celebrations last week. The Phillies had to be feeling good with a 1-0 lead for a couple innings there, until the Braves essentially ended the game with 8 runs in the fourth inning. Ronald Acuna kicked things off with a towering homer (and a normal home run trot).

La Bestia mode activated 🔥#LocalFordDealer | @ronaldacunajr24 pic.twitter.com/blKPAhoG0w

The Braves then got a walk, single, single, single, error, wild pitch, walk, double, and single to score another 7 runs. Drake Baldwin provided the double before things got all the way back around to Acuna for the last single, bringing home the last run of the inning.

Mahle continued to cruise after that Harper homer, finishing 7.0 innings of 1-run ball with no walks, even though he only had 7 whiffs and 3 strikeouts. The Braves added another run on in the sixth with a Ronald ABS strikeout-turned-walk, an error on an Olson ground ball, and an Ozzie sac fly. The Phillies got one back with a solo homer from Crawford in the eighth against Brent Suter. The Braves got another 3 runs against the position-player pitcher for Philly in the eighth, as Kiersey singled, Albies doubled, and Harris hit a homer off the right field foul pole. Suter finished off the Phillies in the ninth, as the Braves only needed to throw Mahle and Suter on the night.
